text: The capital of Germany is Berlin, a major European political and cultural center.
The boiling point of water under standard atmospheric pressure is 100 degrees Celsius.
Neil Armstrong was the first person to walk on the Moon, during the Apollo 11 mission in July 1969.
The Mona Lisa was painted by Leonardo da Vinci in the early 16th century and is displayed at the Louvre in Paris.
Jupiter is the largest planet in the Solar System by both mass and volume.
The Nile is generally regarded as the longest river in the world, flowing through northeastern Africa.
William Shakespeare wrote plays including Hamlet, Macbeth, and Romeo and Juliet in the late 16th and early 17th centuries.
The United Nations was founded in 1945 to promote international cooperation and peace.
A standard year has 365 days, and a leap year has 366 days to keep the calendar aligned with Earth's orbit.
The human brain contains roughly 86 billion neurons, according to modern neuroscience estimates.
HTML, CSS, and JavaScript are the core technologies used to build web pages.
The periodic table organizes chemical elements by increasing atomic number.
The French Revolution began in 1789 and led to major political and social change in France.
Antarctica is the coldest, driest, and windiest continent on Earth and is not permanently inhabited by any nation's civilian population.
Charles Darwin proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection, published in On the Origin of Species in 1859.
The Great Barrier Reef, located off the coast of Queensland, Australia, is the world's largest coral reef system.
Mount Kilimanjaro in Tanzania is the highest mountain in Africa.
The printing press, developed by Johannes Gutenberg around 1440, greatly increased the spread of written information in Europe.
